children: The FTSE 100 gained more than 0.5% on Thursday, with investors focused on the Bank of England’s interest-rate decision following the Federal Reserve’s move the previous day.
The Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, as widely expected, and signalled another increase later this year, a decision that drew criticism from President Donald Trump.
Meanwhile, oil prices declined for a second consecutive session, potentially easing some pressure on UK gilt markets, although trading could remain cautious ahead of the BoE announcement.
Next led the index, rising more than 2% after the retailer raised its full-year guidance.
The company cited a modest improvement in sales expectations and additional cost savings, particularly in warehousing.
Banks also advanced, with HSBC Holdings up 1.1% and Barclays gaining 0.9%.
AstraZeneca and GSK each rose more than 1%, while Unilever added 0.5%.
Rolls-Royce gained 2% and British American Tobacco climbed 1.4%, supporting the broader market.

title: FTSE 100 Rises Ahead BoE
